hypothesised_benefit_and_arm: Arm C (cytokine, engine arm, H_HARM): NRF2 represses Il6 and Il1b transcription (PMID 27211851) so activation lowers them IF they are harmful AND a cytokine-expressing compartment exists. discriminating_test: Step 0 gate then step 1 (README section 6): NRF2 nuclear protein, NQO1 activity, ROS and cytokine PROTEIN in WWOX-deficient vs isogenic corrected human neural cells, with microglia in the system; then NFE2L2-dependence-controlled activation (KEAP1 knockdown, omaveloxolone, MMF) with viability, network activity, lipid peroxidation
wwox_observation: No NRF2 pathway datum in any WWOX-deficient neural cell. Neural-adjacent: Drosophila neuronal Wwox knockdown raises mitochondrial H2O2 (PMC13684411, roGFP2-Orp1, t 3.221, p 0.0047, N 9-11). Non-neural: Wwox-null MEF late-passage ROS up, NAC rescues senescence escape; early-passage redox-gene transcripts up (PMC10613160). Human KO organoid: NFE2L2 0.75x, NQO1 0.73x, HMOX1 1.67x, SRXN1 1.33x, G6PD 0.75x (cpm ratio, 4 v 2 libraries, one deposit, no coherent signature); IL1B/IL6/TNF essentially absent (raw counts 0-11)
external_precedent: CDDO-EA (an analogue, NOT omaveloxolone) lowers IL-6/IL-1b/TNF mRNA, MDA, and delays spontaneous seizures after kainate-SE in adult rat (PMC13701765; Nrf2 target engagement NOT measured; cytokine effect gone at 10 weeks). DMF antiepileptogenic in kainate rat (abstract-level, from IT9 P4c-D). Not transferable between molecules
counter_evidence: Il6 is the only significant cytokine in the null hippocampus (about 1.48x, n 4, one asterisk) and Tnf-a is NOT (about 1.85x, large SEM, no mark); P47T cerebellum IL1B/TNF >=2x (n 6, transcript, overlaps WT range); rat lde/lde glia LOWER; human organoid has no cytokine-expressing cells; Kobayashi: NRF2 leaves Tnf unchanged and the work is bone-marrow macrophages, not microglia; NRF2 expression adult brain is highest in macrophage/astrocyte (HPA, IT9 file); brain Nrf2 induction in monkey modest; omaveloxolone developmental toxicity (below)
missing_data: NRF2 protein/target activity and ROS in WWOX-deficient neural cells; cytokine protein and caspase-1 maturation anywhere in WWOX models; numeric omaveloxolone potency in neural cells; free (unbound) brain concentration (protein binding 97%); microglial/astrocytic NRF2 response to the compound; any WWOX-model response
